summary: Monaco's government says visitors need the passport, and any visa, required to enter France: EEA citizens need only a valid passport or identity card, visa-exempt nationalities can stay under 90 days, and others need a Schengen visa from the embassy of the Schengen country through which they enter Europe. The UK says France handles immigration matters for Monaco and that days there count within the Schengen 90-day limit.

passportValidity.text: The UK says Monaco follows Schengen area rules: a passport must have an expiry date at least 3 months after the day you plan to leave the Schengen area and have been issued within the last 10 years. Monaco's government says EEA citizens only need a valid passport or identity card.

travelInsurance.text: Monaco runs no check of its own, but France lists insurance covering medical and hospital costs in France, with minimum cover of €30,000, among the conditions every non-EU visitor must meet at the border, visa-free or not. Schengen visa applicants must also show travel medical insurance of at least €30,000 valid across the Schengen Area.

proofOfFunds.text: Monaco runs no check of its own, but France applies its means-of-subsistence rule at the border to every non-EU visitor, visa-free or not. You need €65 per day with a hotel booking, €120 per day without proof of accommodation, or €32.50 per day with a host certificate (attestation d'accueil). Other Schengen countries set their own amounts if you enter through them.

tips.text: Monaco's government says foreign visitors staying less than three months must hold the passport, and any visa, required to enter France; EEA nationals need a valid passport or identity card.
The UK says the Schengen area includes Monaco for its 90-days-in-180 visa-free limit, so days in Monaco count together with time in other Schengen countries.
The UK says you could be fined in Monaco for walking around in swimsuits, stripped to the waist or barefoot anywhere except beaches and bathing areas.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Monaco?
faq.answer: Monaco's government says visitors need the passport, and any visa, required to enter France. EEA citizens need only a valid passport or identity card; visa-exempt nationalities such as the US, UK and Japan can stay under 90 days; and others need a Schengen visa from the embassy of the Schengen country through which they enter Europe, after which Monaco can be visited without other formalities.

faq.question: Is Monaco in the Schengen Area?
faq.answer: The UK says Monaco follows Schengen area rules and that France handles immigration matters for Monaco. Monaco's government says visitors need the passport, and any visa, required to enter France.

faq.question: Do I need my passport for a day trip from Nice to Monaco?
faq.answer: Monaco's government says foreign visitors must hold the passport, and any visa, required to enter France, and that EEA nationals need a valid passport or identity card. No official source we could read says when identity is checked on the way into Monaco.

faq.question: How can I stay in Monaco longer than 90 days?
faq.answer: Monaco's government says anyone aged 16 or over who wishes to stay in Monaco for more than three months a year must apply to the Monegasque authorities for a residence card (carte de séjour), after obtaining a visa or establishment authorisation and with proof of accommodation and sufficient resources.

faq.question: How long can US citizens stay in Monaco?
faq.answer: The UK government says the Schengen area includes Monaco for its visa-free limit of 90 days in any 180-day period, and that visits to other Schengen countries count towards the 90 days.
